subject: Extract mean for a binned dataset

messages.author: fa51e47cdd090afc
messages.subject: Extract mean for a binned dataset
parts:
Hi all,
I'm currently analyzing a huge dataset that comes from binned sets from different tissues and slides. I've done it in Cardinal 1.10. Those are old datasets analyzed a time ago...
I've done normalization and bin over 15 tissues.
Then, I've combined them using combine method and now i want to extract the mean for each mass for each tissue but i'm stuck with this because i don't know how to extract them.
I want to extract a csv where the column names are each separated sample and in the row names is the mean intensity for this binned mass.
Any suggestion is welcome!

messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Extract mean for a binned dataset
parts:
Here are a few approaches:

library(Cardinal)
data(rcc, package="CardinalWorkflows")
rcc2 <- as(rcc.small, "MSImagingExperiment")


# version 2.4
rcc.sm <- summarize(rcc2, .stat="mean", .groups=run(rcc2), .as="DataFrame")


# version 2.6 (upcoming release)
rcc.agg <- aggregate(rcc2, FUN="mean", groups=run(rcc2), as="DataFrame")


# using matter
rcc.rs <- matter::rowStats(spectra(rcc2), stat="mean", groups=run(rcc2))


-Kylie

messages.subject: Re: Extract mean for a binned dataset
parts:
Thanks Kylie!!! I have to recognize that i have a problem with R scripting. Maybe I need to think in a simple way ;)

I've also other (more complicated and tedious, hahahahaha!!!) solution:

#extract iData:
write.csv(data@imageData@data$iData, file="pixels_idata.csv")

#names of columns (pixels):
pixels<- data@imageData@dimnames[[2]]

#read csv and assign colnames to every pixel (colname consists in a string like "x=..., y=..., sample=....")
intensity<-read.csv("pixels_idata.csv", col.names = pixels)

#filter data to extract pixels from same sample

data_subset<- intensity %>% select(contains("put_here_sampleName"))

write.csv(data_subset, file="sample_subset.csv")

#Then you can calculate the mean for each subset
